summary.en: Some things are within our power, some are not.
summary.zh: 有些事在我们能力之内，有些不在。

what.en: The dichotomy of control divides everything into what is up to us — our judgments, desires, aversions — and what is not — our bodies, possessions, reputation. Epictetus opens the Enchiridion with it.
what.zh: 控制二分法把一切分为在我们能力之内者——判断、欲望、厌恶——与不在者——身体、财产、名声。爱比克泰德以此开篇《手册》。

why.en: It is the foundation of all Stoic practice: peace comes from investing concern only where you have power, and releasing the rest.
why.zh: 它是一切斯多葛实践的根基：唯将关切投于能力所及处、放下其余，方得安宁。

position.en: It grounds tranquility — once internalized, the path to ataraxia opens. Nearly every other practice depends on it.
position.zh: 它支撑着安宁——一旦内化，通往不动心之路即开。几乎所有其他实践都依赖于它。

quote.en: Some things are within our power, while others are not.
quote.zh: 有些事物在我们的能力范围之内，有些则不在。

summary.en: Freedom from being disturbed by what you cannot change.
summary.zh: 不为不可改变之事所扰的自由。

what.en: Tranquility (ataraxia) is freedom from disturbance — not passivity, but the calm that follows from no longer being shaken by what lies outside your control.
what.zh: 安宁（不动心）是免于扰动——非消极，而是不再为控制之外之事所动摇后的平静。

why.en: It is the practical payoff of Stoic philosophy: the state a practitioner aims toward.
why.zh: 它是斯多葛哲学的实践回报：修习者所趋向的状态。

position.en: Tranquility follows from the dichotomy of control and is sustained by the cardinal virtues. It is mentioned across both source notes.
position.zh: 安宁源于控制二分法，由四枢德所维系。两份笔记中皆有提及。

quote.en: Tranquility is not passivity; it is freedom from being disturbed.
quote.zh: 安宁非消极，而是免于被扰动的自由。

summary.en: Rehearsing misfortune in advance to rob it of its power to shock.
summary.zh: 预先演练不幸，以剥夺其令人震惊的力量。

what.en: Premeditatio malorum is the exercise of vividly imagining loss, hardship, or death before it arrives, so that when adversity comes it finds you already prepared.
what.zh: 预想逆境（premeditatio malorum）是在不幸来临前生动想象失去、艰难或死亡的练习，使逆境到来时你已有准备。

why.en: It turns the dichotomy of control from a belief into a daily habit — Seneca recommended it constantly.
why.zh: 它把控制二分法从信念变为日常习惯——塞内卡反复推荐。

position.en: A concrete practice that applies the dichotomy of control and cultivates tranquility.
position.zh: 一种应用控制二分法、培养安宁的具体实践。

quote.en: He robs present ills of their power who has perceived their coming beforehand.
quote.zh: 预见祸患将至者，已先夺其威。

what.en: The four cardinal virtues are wisdom (knowing good from bad), justice (our dealings with others), courage (endurance in difficulty), and temperance (moderation of desire).
what.zh: 四枢德为智慧（辨善恶）、正义（待人之道）、勇气（困中之坚忍）、节制（欲望之节度）。

why.en: For the Stoics virtue is the ONLY true good and is sufficient for happiness — this is the ethical core.
why.zh: 于斯多葛而言，德是唯一真正的善，且足以致幸福——此为其伦理核心。

position.en: The virtues sustain tranquility and stand in contrast to preferred indifferents (external goods).
position.zh: 诸德维系安宁，与‘可取的无关者’（外在之物）形成对照。

summary.en: External goods worth having but not necessary for a good life.
summary.zh: 值得拥有、但非美好生活所必需的外在之物。

what.en: Preferred indifferents are things like wealth and health: worth pursuing, but not constitutive of happiness. Their absence cannot make a virtuous life bad.
what.zh: 可取的无关者如财富与健康：值得追求，却不构成幸福。其缺失不能使有德之生变坏。

why.en: This concept is what separates Stoicism from Aristotle, who held external goods to be partly constitutive of flourishing.
why.zh: 此概念正是斯多葛与亚里士多德的分野——后者认为外在之物部分地构成繁盛。

position.en: Contrasts with the cardinal virtues: virtue is necessary and sufficient, indifferents are neither.
position.zh: 与四枢德相对照：德为必要且充分，无关者二者皆非。

quote.en: External goods are preferred, but not necessary for a good life.
quote.zh: 外在之善为可取，却非美好生活所必需。
